messages:

Subject: Post-call: Redwood vs hyperscaler demo matrix & next tests

Hi Alex — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps plan so we can make the bake-off productive for your infra and procurement teams.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary objective: evaluate inference economics + reliability for real-time features (p50 latency target ~150ms for 256-token responses; sustained throughput target ~200 reqs/s).
- Constraints: must support VPC peering or private deployment (data residency), SOC 2 evidence required, and predictable unit cost for modeling forecasts.
- Hyperscaler concerns you raised: cold-start variability, noisy-neighbor degradation during multi-tenant bursts, and opaque per-token billing that complicates forecasts.

Proposed hands-on tests (attached "redwood-demo-matrix.xlsx"):
1) Latency profile: 256-token generation @ variable concurrency (10, 50, 200) — measure p50/p90/p99 and tail behavior across 30-minute runs.
2) Throughput & stability: sustained 1-hour 200 reqs/s run with KV cache enabled vs disabled to quantify cost delta.
3) Cost projection exercise: run a traced sample workload (10k sessions) and produce a per-month cost model (tokens + infra).
4) Failover/fallback test: route a subset of traffic to a smaller quantized variant to validate graceful degradation and quality drop.
5) Integration smoke: SSO via SAML, and one-shot file upload to ensure private deployment fits your network.

Owners we suggest: me (coord + procurement), Vivek (benchmarks/runbook), Marissa (pricing + success criteria). Proposed timeline: week of Oct 25 — smoke tests; Nov 1 — full throughput runs; decision checkpoint Nov 8.

Please confirm people to include in the test runs (engineering contact, procurement contact) and whether the week of Oct 25 works. I attached the demo matrix and a short decision-criteria doc.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

- We need an initial cost projection that includes peak-day and average-month assumptions; if you can provide a template we will plug in our session counts.
- SLA examples and incident response commitments would be helpful to share with procurement.

Week of Oct 25 looks good for smoke tests. Primary engineering contact will be me (I’ll loop in our infra lead after we confirm the SSO details). Procurement contact: procurement@nimbus.ai.

Looping you both in with Alex's note — procurement@nimbus.ai has asked for Azure VNet compatibility and SLA examples. Quick internal plan so we stay aligned: 

Proposed owners + asks:
- Marissa: own pricing model and provide the cost-projection template (deliverable: cost_template.xlsx) — due Oct 22 so Alex can pre-populate.
- Vivek: own the benchmark harness and runbook (deliverable: runbook.md + scripts) — prepare tests for Oct 25 smoke window. Note we should include a small cold-start microbenchmark to show hyperscaler variance.
- Karthik: coordinate SOW/procurement questions and draft SLA examples; also manage the HubSpot timeline and exec touchpoints.

Decision criteria (short):
- Latency: p50 <= 150ms for target sequence length; p99 behavior documented.
- Cost: clear per-1M token baseline with estimated monthly spend (3 scenarios: baseline/expected/peak).
- Reliability: no >10% degradation in p50 under burst testing; acceptable fallback quality when using quantized variants.
- Integration: SSO + VNet peering validated for private deployment.

Timeline reminders:
- Oct 22: pricing template to Alex
- Oct 25: smoke tests (SSO + small latency runs)
- Nov 1: 1-hour throughput & stability run
- Nov 8: decision checkpoint with Nimbus execs

Any objections or missing items? If all good I’ll send Alex a short calendar invite for the Oct 25 window and link the runbook in HubSpot.

—K
